meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (J560/01, Friday 19 May 2023), downloaded from www.ocr.org.uk. Derived metadata only — question numbers, marks, mark-scheme codes and skill tags. No exam question text transcribed.
meta.note: Third OCR series. As always with OCR there is no per-question total printed, only a bare [N] against each part, so the whole-paper sum is the only check available: 49 markers summing to exactly the printed 100. Coded WITH mark_split, derived from OCR's part totals and partial-credit routes rather than quoted.

coding_notes: mark_split for OCR is DERIVED, not transcribed — see OCR-JUN24-F-P1 for the reasoning. q21 is recorded as B4 because every route OCR prints for it (listing tram times, listing multiples, stating the LCM) is B-coded; there is a single M1 alternative for prime factorisation, so that row slightly understates method marks.

q12 (surface area of a cuboid) tagged areas_of_squares_and_rectangles, the documented handling for that taxonomy gap — spheres, cones and cylinders each have a surface-area node and cuboids do not, and the mark scheme rewards finding rectangle areas and doubling.

q2 tagged range, median and factors_and_multiples together: the mark scheme awards B3/B2/B1 purely by how many of the three stated conditions the four numbers satisfy, so all three are genuinely exercised by one answer.
q26 is y = 6/x - 2x, a two-branch curve, not a quadratic — tagged sketching_functions. The table in the paper confirms it (x = -4 gives 6.5, x = 4 gives -6.5).

q10a and q10b are both 'spot the error' items but on different nodes: (a) is an incorrect inverse operation when solving, (b) is substituting the final velocity where the initial one belongs. Tagged solving_linear_equations and substitution respectively.

q22a and q22b tagged direct_proportion: the first asks what about a straight line through the origin shows proportionality, and the second adds a parallel line with a positive intercept, which is the contrast.
